correctness.rationale: With the stipulated left-to-right concatenation, left multiplication preserves terminal vertex. In the basis e_(i+2), a_(i+1), b_i the only possibly nonzero entries are x_(i+1), y_i, x_i below the diagonal, and the square has single possibly nonzero entry x_i x_(i+1). A nonzero square forces a size-three block, the zero matrix forces three size-one blocks, and all other cases have one size-two and one size-one block. Charge each nonzero x_i once on its outgoing support edge; independently summing y_i gives the four transfer entries, with the trace counting labeled cyclic sequences exactly once. The normalization is q^(2n); a proper run of a+1 nonzero x_i realizes exactly a adjacent pairs for 0<=a<=n-2, and any zero destroys at least two edges. The no-size-three event is a weighted cycle independent-set count; the eigenvalues are the roots of lambda²-lambda-(q-1), with |lambda_-|<lambda_+<q for q>=2. For covariance the single-site means are p² and r³, each same-type neighbor has joint expectation p³ or r⁵ respectively, and there are three disjoint-in-value overlapping cross terms per site, including at n=3. All other windows depend on disjoint underlying variables. This gives the stated matrix and determinant p³r⁴(r+4). After removing the seam and one site between consecutive blocks of length floor(n^(1/3)), retained scalar directional block sums are independent and uniformly o(sqrt n). The discarded variance is O(n^(2/3)) by finite dependence, so Lindeberg and Cramér–Wold give the claimed fixed-q limit. There is no rate claim. Independent exact rank and census replay on all elements at (q,n)=(2,3),(2,5),(4,3), using GF(4) arithmetic for the last case, also compared the cross-covariance and checked the determinant symbolically (python3 /workspace/branches/independent_replay.py 5). The frozen prime-field verifier was inspected, not executed. Neither replay proves the general limit.

value.rationale: The regular action's finite-field Jordan partition is a natural invariant of this constrained family. The exact narrow census is also available in the later catalog record, but the evaluated joint statistics provide a useful additional description: exact finite means and cross-covariance, strictly positive determinant, and a normal law governing the full block-count vector at fixed q. The negative covariance and the explicit cubic-radical block parameters come from the overlapping windows, not from unrestricted triangular ensembles. The value is this concrete statistical refinement of a natural algebraic invariant, not a claim of a general CLT or of a convergence rate.
